title: Gradients for a whole network, and a way to trust them
brief: Wire the engine into a two-layer network, then write the finite-difference check that tells you the gradients are right.
hints: mlp_loss_and_grad: wrap every W and b in a fresh Tensor, compute h @ W + b for each layer, apply .relu() on every layer except the last, call softmax_cross_entropy on the last output, call backward() once, then copy each .grad.
numeric_grad: copy the array, and for each entry (np.ndindex helps) nudge it up by h, measure the loss, nudge it down by h, measure the loss, restore it, and record (high - low) / (2h).

gradient_check: for each parameter array, compare the analytic gradient with numeric_grad. Use norm(analytic - numeric) / (norm(analytic) + norm(numeric)), and return the largest value over all arrays.
Inside numeric_grad's loss function, build a new params list with only that one array replaced, and return only the loss from mlp_loss_and_grad.
